chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: The grind of theatre shows
summary: Five or six shows a day, starting at ten in the morning, weeks at a time with the movie.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, that must have been something, though, the grind of doing those shows.
How many shows a day did you do?
Five or six shows a day.
On the weekend it was more, right?
And it would start at ten o'clock.

In the morning, yeah. And sometimes you'd get out at 12 o'clock at night. Then sometimes, you'd meet yourself coming back on the stage just after they'd close the curtain, and they'd say, "Curtain time," and the curtain starts opening up again and you've got to start all over again. You'd say, "God-damn, wait a minute."
Now, how many weeks would you do? One or two?
Oh, shit, it might be ten weeks you would be there.
With the movie, right? Running the movie.
Running the movie, you know. So that was a helluva thing, man. Shit, they'd work you to death.
